audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for temple prediction, Olivet discourse, birth-pains, persecution, abomination/desolation, false messiahs, cosmic signs, Son of Humanity, fig tree, unknown day/hour, and watchfulness.

verses.restored: As he was going out from the temple, one of his disciples said to him, Teacher, look, what stones and what buildings!

familiar.text: And as he went out of the temple, one of his disciples saith unto him, Master, see what manner of stones and what buildings are here!

modern.text: As Jesus was leaving the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, “Teacher, look at the magnificent stones and buildings!”

original.text: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ λέγει αὐτῷ εἷς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ· Διδάσκαλε, ἴδε ποταποὶ λίθοι καὶ ποταπαὶ οἰκοδομαί.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be thrown down.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said unto him, Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

modern.text: “Do you see all these great buildings?” Jesus replied. “Not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”

original.text: καὶ ὁ ⸀Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Βλέπεις ταύτας τὰς μεγάλας οἰκοδομάς; οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ ⸀ὧδε λίθος ἐπὶ ⸀λίθον ὃς οὐ μὴ καταλυθῇ.

verses.restored: As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew questioned him privately,

familiar.text: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately,

modern.text: While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked Him privately,

original.text: Καὶ καθημένου αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν κατέναντι τοῦ ἱεροῦ ⸀ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν κατʼ ἰδίαν Πέτρος καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἀνδρέας·

verses.restored: Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be completed?

familiar.text: Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when all these things shall be fulfilled?

modern.text: “Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to be fulfilled?”

original.text: Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν πότε ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ⸂ταῦτα συντελεῖσθαι πάντα⸃.

verses.restored: Jesus began to say to them, See that no one leads you astray.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering them began to say, Take heed lest any man deceive you:

modern.text: Jesus began by telling them, “See to it that no one deceives you.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸂ἤρξατο λέγειν αὐτοῖς⸃· Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς πλανήσῃ·

verses.restored: Many will come in my name, saying, I am, and they will lead many astray.

familiar.text: For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.

modern.text: Many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and will deceive many.

original.text: ⸀πολλοὶ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσιν.

verses.restored: When you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be troubled; these things must happen, but the end is not yet.

familiar.text: And when ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars, be ye not troubled: for such things must needs be; but the end shall not be yet.

modern.text: When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is still to come.

original.text: ὅταν δὲ ⸀ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκοὰς πολέμων, μὴ θροεῖσθε· ⸀δεῖ γενέσθαι, ἀλλʼ οὔπω τὸ τέλος.

verses.restored: Nation will rise against nation and reign against reign; there will be earthquakes in various places, and famines. These are the beginning of birth-pains.

familiar.text: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be earthquakes in divers places, and there shall be famines and troubles: these are the beginnings of sorrows.

modern.text: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places, as well as famines. These are the beginning of birth pains. Witnessing to All Nations (Matthew 24:9–14; Luke 21:10–19)

original.text: ἐγερθήσεται γὰρ ἔθνος ἐπʼ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν, ⸀ἔσονται σεισμοὶ κατὰ τόπους, ⸁ἔσονται ⸀λιμοί· ⸀ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων ταῦτα.

verses.restored: But you, watch yourselves. They will hand you over to councils, and you will be beaten in synagogues; you will stand before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them.

familiar.text: But take heed to yourselves: for they shall deliver you up to councils; and in the synagogues ye shall be beaten: and ye shall be brought before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them.

modern.text: So be on your guard. You will be delivered over to the councils and beaten in the synagogues. On My account you will stand before governors and kings as witnesses to them.

original.text: βλέπετε δὲ ὑμεῖς ἑαυτούς· ⸀παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια καὶ εἰς συναγωγὰς δαρήσεσθε καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνων καὶ βασιλέων σταθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: The good message must first be proclaimed to all nations.

familiar.text: And the gospel must first be published among all nations.

modern.text: And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.

original.text: καὶ εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ⸂πρῶτον δεῖ⸃ κηρυχθῆναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον.

verses.restored: When they lead you away and hand you over, do not worry beforehand what you should speak; but whatever is given to you in that hour, speak that, for it is not you speaking but the holy Spirit.

familiar.text: But when they shall lead you, and deliver you up, take no thought beforehand what ye shall speak, neither do ye premeditate: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye: for it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Ghost.

modern.text: But when they arrest you and hand you over, do not worry beforehand what to say. Instead, speak whatever you are given at that time, for it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.

original.text: ⸂καὶ ὅταν⸃ ⸀ἄγωσιν ὑμᾶς παραδιδόντες, μὴ προμεριμνᾶτε τί ⸀λαλήσητε, ἀλλʼ ὃ ἐὰν δοθῇ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦτο λαλεῖτε, οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑμεῖς οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον.

verses.restored: Brother will hand over brother to death, and father child; children will rise against parents and put them to death.

familiar.text: Now the brother shall betray the brother to death, and the father the son; and children shall rise up against their parents, and shall cause them to be put to death.

modern.text: Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.

original.text: ⸂καὶ παραδώσει⸃ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς·

verses.restored: You will be hated by all because of my name, but the one enduring to the end will be saved.

familiar.text: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.

modern.text: You will be hated by everyone because of My name, but the one who perseveres to the end will be saved. The Abomination of Desolation (Matthew 24:15–25; Luke 21:20–24)

original.text: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου. ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.

verses.restored: When you see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not, let the reader understand, then those in Judea must flee to the mountains.

familiar.text: But when ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not, (let him that readeth understand,) then let them that be in Judaea flee to the mountains:

modern.text: So when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be (let the reader understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.

original.text: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως ⸀ἑστηκότα ὅπου οὐ δεῖ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω, τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη,

verses.restored: The one on the roof must not go down or enter to take anything out of the house.

familiar.text: And let him that is on the housetop not go down into the house, neither enter therein, to take any thing out of his house:

modern.text: Let no one on the housetop go back inside to retrieve anything from his house.

original.text: ⸀ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ ⸀καταβάτω μηδὲ εἰσελθάτω ⸂τι ἆραι⸃ ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: The one in the field must not turn back to take the cloak.

familiar.text: And let him that is in the field not turn back again for to take up his garment.

modern.text: And let no one in the field return for his cloak.

original.text: καὶ ὁ εἰς τὸν ⸀ἀγρὸν μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω ἆραι τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Woe to those carrying in the womb and nursing infants in those days.

familiar.text: But woe to them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days!

modern.text: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!

original.text: οὐαὶ δὲ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.

verses.restored: Pray that it may not happen in winter.

familiar.text: And pray ye that your flight be not in the winter.

modern.text: Pray that this will not occur in the winter.

original.text: προσεύχεσθε δὲ ἵνα μὴ ⸀γένηται χειμῶνος·

verses.restored: For those days will be pressure such as has not happened from the beginning of creation that the Divine created until now, and will not happen again.

familiar.text: For in those days shall be affliction, such as was not from the beginning of the creation which God created unto this time, neither shall be.

modern.text: For those will be days of tribulation unmatched from the beginning of God’s creation until now, and never to be seen again.

original.text: ἔσονται γὰρ αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι θλῖψις οἵα οὐ γέγονεν τοιαύτη ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως ⸀ἣν ἔκτισεν ὁ θεὸς ἕως τοῦ νῦν καὶ οὐ μὴ γένηται.

verses.restored: Unless the Lord shortened the days, no flesh would be saved; but because of the chosen whom he chose, he shortened the days.

familiar.text: And except that the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh should be saved: but for the elect’s sake, whom he hath chosen, he hath shortened the days.

modern.text: If the Lord had not cut short those days, nobody would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen, He has cut them short.

original.text: καὶ εἰ μὴ ⸂ἐκολόβωσεν κύριος⸃ τὰς ἡμέρας, οὐκ ἂν ἐσώθη πᾶσα σάρξ. ἀλλὰ διὰ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἐκολόβωσεν τὰς ἡμέρας.

verses.restored: Then if anyone says to you, Look, here is the Messiah, or, Look, there, do not trust it.

familiar.text: And then if any man shall say to you, Lo, here is Christ; or, lo, he is there; believe him not:

modern.text: At that time if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.

original.text: ⸀καὶ τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· ⸀Ἴδε ὧδε ὁ ⸀χριστός, ⸁Ἴδε ἐκεῖ, μὴ πιστεύετε·

verses.restored: For false messiahs and false prophets will arise and give signs and wonders, to lead astray, if possible, the chosen.

familiar.text: For false Christs and false prophets shall rise, and shall shew signs and wonders, to seduce, if it were possible, even the elect.

modern.text: For false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform signs and wonders that would deceive even the elect, if that were possible.

original.text: ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ δώσουσιν σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα πρὸς τὸ ἀποπλανᾶν εἰ ⸀δυνατὸν τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς·

verses.restored: But you, watch; I have told you all things beforehand.

familiar.text: But take ye heed: behold, I have foretold you all things.

modern.text: So be on your guard; I have told you everything in advance. The Return of the Son of Man (Matthew 24:26–31; Luke 21:25–28)

original.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ βλέπετε· ⸀προείρηκα ὑμῖν πάντα.

verses.restored: But in those days, after that pressure, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.

familiar.text: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light,

modern.text: But in those days, after that tribulation: ‘The sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light;

original.text: Ἀλλὰ ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις μετὰ τὴν θλῖψιν ἐκείνην ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται, καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς,

verses.restored: The stars will be falling from heaven, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.

familiar.text: And the stars of heaven shall fall, and the powers that are in heaven shall be shaken.

modern.text: the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.’

original.text: καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες ⸂ἔσονται ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πίπτοντες⸃, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς σαλευθήσονται.

verses.restored: Then they will see the Son of Humanity coming in clouds with great power and glory.

familiar.text: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.

modern.text: At that time they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.

original.text: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλαις μετὰ δυνάμεως πολλῆς καὶ δόξης·

verses.restored: Then he will send the messengers and gather his chosen from the four winds, from the end of earth to the end of heaven.

familiar.text: And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.

modern.text: And He will send out the angels to gather His elect from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven. The Lesson of the Fig Tree (Matthew 24:32–35; Luke 21:29–33)

original.text: καὶ τότε ἀποστελεῖ τοὺς ⸀ἀγγέλους καὶ ἐπισυνάξει τοὺς ⸀ἐκλεκτοὺς ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων ἀπʼ ἄκρου γῆς ἕως ἄκρου οὐρανοῦ.

verses.restored: From the fig tree learn the parable: when its branch becomes tender and puts out leaves, you know summer is near.

familiar.text: Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When her branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is near:

modern.text: Now learn this lesson from the fig tree: As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.

original.text: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς συκῆς μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν· ὅταν ⸂ἤδη ὁ κλάδος αὐτῆς⸃ ἁπαλὸς γένηται καὶ ἐκφύῃ τὰ φύλλα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·

verses.restored: So also, when you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the doors.

familiar.text: So ye in like manner, when ye shall see these things come to pass, know that it is nigh, even at the doors.

modern.text: So also, when you see these things happening, know that He is near, right at the door.

original.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ⸂ἴδητε ταῦτα⸃ γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἐπὶ θύραις.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things happen.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, that this generation shall not pass, till all these things be done.

modern.text: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.

original.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη μέχρις οὗ ⸂ταῦτα πάντα⸃ γένηται.

verses.restored: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.

familiar.text: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

modern.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away. Readiness at Any Hour (Matthew 24:36–51; Luke 12:35–48)

original.text: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ ⸀παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ ⸀μὴ ⸁παρελεύσονται.

verses.restored: Concerning that day or hour, no one knows, not the messengers in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father.

familiar.text: But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.

modern.text: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.

original.text: Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ἢ ⸀τῆς ὥρας οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ οἱ ἄγγελοι ⸀ἐν οὐρανῷ οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός, εἰ μὴ ὁ πατήρ.

verses.restored: Watch; stay awake. For you do not know when the time is.

familiar.text: Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.

modern.text: Be on your guard and stay alert! For you do not know when the appointed time will come.

original.text: βλέπετε ⸀ἀγρυπνεῖτε, οὐκ οἴδατε γὰρ πότε ὁ καιρός ἐστιν·

verses.restored: It is like a person away on a journey, who left his house, gave authority to his servants, to each one the work, and commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.

familiar.text: For the Son of man is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.

modern.text: It is like a man going on a journey who left his house, put each servant in charge of his own task, and instructed the doorkeeper to keep watch.

original.text: ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀπόδημος ἀφεὶς τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ καὶ δοὺς τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐξουσίαν, ⸀ἑκάστῳ τὸ ἔργον αὐτοῦ, καὶ τῷ θυρωρῷ ἐνετείλατο ἵνα γρηγορῇ.

verses.restored: Therefore keep watch, for you do not know when the lord of the house comes: evening, midnight, rooster-sound, or morning,

familiar.text: Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning:

modern.text: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know when the master of the house will return—whether in the evening, at midnight, when the rooster crows, or in the morning.

original.text: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, οὐκ οἴδατε γὰρ πότε ὁ κύριος τῆς οἰκίας ἔρχεται, ⸀ἢ ὀψὲ ἢ ⸀μεσονύκτιον ἢ ἀλεκτοροφωνίας ἢ πρωΐ,

verses.restored: lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.

familiar.text: Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.

modern.text: Otherwise, he may arrive without notice and find you sleeping.

original.text: μὴ ἐλθὼν ἐξαίφνης εὕρῃ ὑμᾶς καθεύδοντας·

verses.restored: What I say to you, I say to all: Keep watch.

familiar.text: And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.

modern.text: And what I say to you, I say to everyone: Keep watch!”

original.text: ⸀ὃ δὲ ὑμῖν λέγω πᾶσιν λέγω· γρηγορεῖτε.
